title: BLITZSCALE: Fast and Live Large Model Autoscaling with O(1) Host Caching
technique: network-based (GPU compute-network multicast) parameter loading for O(1)-cached autoscaling plus layer-level live scaling with ZigZag pipeline scheduling

optimized_metrics.evidence: There are three metrics to minimize for the generation: (1) the scale time, (2) the plan generation time, and (3) the ...
Under real-world workloads, our system BLITZSCALE achieves up to 94 % lower tail latency reductions compared to state-of-the-art autoscaling system (ServerlessLLM)
observed a 1.5x longer scale time and 50% degraded tail TBT ... ZigZag pipeline scheduling and achieve 50% tail latency reduction under bursty workloads
Autoscaling speed is critical in minimizing SLO violations because the queued requests are not served until the instances are scaled.
it reduces the GPU time used for serving by 49 % when compared with serving systems that do not support autoscaling like DistServe and vLLM with the same service-level-agreement
trade-off between scaling speed and storage/memory usage to cache parameters ... no or O(1) caching

headline_claim.text: up to 94 % lower tail latency reductions compared to ServerlessLLM, and reduces the GPU time used for serving by 49 % compared with serving systems that do not support autoscaling like DistServe and vLLM with the same service-level-agreement

metric_definitions.definition_quote: SLO defines the tolerable end-to-end latency measured from the time a request is sent to the system to the time the inference response is returned. Thus, the latency includes the queueing delays waiting for the scaled instance to be ready for inference.
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT includes queueing; prefill evaluated with TTFT, decode with TBT

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We follow the traditional 5 x SLO [81] ... if a request's end-to-end (TTFT or TBT) latency is exceeds 5 x the average latency, it violates the SLO.
metric_definitions.notes: SLO = 5x average latency, per TTFT and TBT
resource usage metric; used as cost proxy

slo_spec: 5x the average TTFT/TBT latency per request counts as violation; also 1250 ms TTFT SLO used in motivation example
load_regime: trace replay (BurstGPT, AzureCode, AzureConv) with PD-disaggregated and colocated setups
tradeoff_acknowledged: BLITZSCALE slightly increases TBT in decode-sufficient cases (TBT gain much smaller than TTFT gain)
hardware: Cluster A (1.6 Tbps NVLink, A800) and Cluster B (256 Gbps PCIe)
extractor_notes: Ambiguous: the system's direct design target is scaling speed (scale time) and caching footprint; latency (TTFT/TBT tail, mean in main plots) and GPU time are the outcome metrics. 'Tail latency' in the abstract not tied to a single percentile; P95 TBT and P99 TTFT appear in figures.
